title: 7 Base44 Alternatives Worth Trying in 2026
summary: 7 Base44 alternatives for business apps, from Lovable and Softr to Bubble and Zite, compared on credit pricing vs flat plans and on export.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


1. Base44 bills on two credit meters at once: message credits for building and integration credits for what the app does once it runs. Both reset monthly, and unused credits expire.
2. Softr and Zite keep everyday app use off the credit meter: Softr's AI credits pay only for AI features and pause them when they run out instead of charging you, and Zite doesn't charge credits for manual edits, visitors or workflow runs from the editor.
3. Export means different things on each tool. Lovable and Replit sync code to GitHub, Zite exports a workspace you can import into another Zite organization, Glide shows code only on Enterprise, and Bubble describes no source-code export.
4. Base44's $16-a-month Starter plan (billed yearly) undercuts the cheapest paid plan of every alternative here, so a working app with steady credit use may cost less staying put.


Base44 turns a plain-words prompt into a working app with its database, logins and hosting attached, which suits internal tools, client portals and trackers. Wix owns it now: Wix bought Base44 in June 2025 for about $80 million plus earn-out payments through 2029, and the site's footer reads "© 2026 Wix.com Ltd."


People search for Base44 alternatives later, once the app is in daily use. Credits run out mid-fix, the bill depends on two meters, and it gets harder to say what you could take with you if you left.


This list judges each tool on those three things: how it prices AI building, what a flat plan actually includes, and what export leaves you holding. It covers seven Base44 AI app builder alternatives for business apps, priced from each vendor's own pricing page on October 8, 2026, with the billing basis stated for every figure.


## Why teams look for Base44 alternatives


Cost control is the theme that keeps coming up. Base44's pricing runs on two meters. Message credits pay for AI building, at roughly 0.5 credits for a simple change, 1 for a small feature and 2 for a complex module, by Base44's own examples. Integration credits pay for runtime services such as LLM calls inside your app, about 1 credit each on the default model.


### Credits spent on fixes


The first meter is the one that stings, because a fix the AI gets wrong still costs credits.


One Base44 user wrote[on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/Base44/comments/1qyw8ax/whats_the_base44_alternative/) that "I've gone through tons of credits trying to fix this," after trying Builder mode, Visual and Discussion, and said the app "STILL shows the first part of the email" instead of the user's name. That's a single user's report, but it's the cost to watch: credits spent on a fix that didn't hold.


Starter's 100 message credits cover about 50 complex modules or 200 simple changes at those example rates. That sounds roomy until a fix needs five attempts.


### The 2025 security disclosure


Some teams also remember July 2025. Wiz Research found that Base44's registration endpoints accepted a non-secret app ID, which let an outsider create a verified account on private apps, including ones set to SSO-only access. Wix fixed it within 24 hours of the July 9 disclosure and found no evidence of past abuse, so it's a resolved incident rather than a live risk.


The lesson applies to every tool below, Base44 included: test who can sign up to a "private" app before you put payroll or customer records in it.


## The best alternatives to Base44, compared


Most alternatives to Base44 AI app builder plans bill some form of credits too, so the table lists each tool's pricing model next to its entry price. The model decides how predictable the bill is. Base44 sits in the last row for reference.


Tool Best for Pricing model (flat vs credits) Main limitation Pricing (from)


Awesomic Studio Ops dashboards and reports, with an expert on call Plan price is the month's usage budget No database or auth claimed, draw-down rate unpublished $20/month, no free plan


Lovable Like-for-like prompt-to-app swap Credits covering building, hosting and in-app AI Monthly-plan credits expire 2 months after issue Free; Pro $21/month billed yearly ($25 monthly)


Softr Client portals on data you already keep Flat plan; AI credits only for AI features 5 team + 5 client logins on Basic Free; Basic $19/month billed yearly ($25 monthly)


Glide Internal apps from a spreadsheet Flat plan plus credits for every prompt GlideOS is in beta, 2 published apps on Basic Free (no published apps); Basic $25/month, billed monthly


Bubble Customer-facing web and mobile apps Flat plan plus AI credits plus workload units No source-code export Free; Starter $29/month billed yearly


Replit Apps a developer will take over Free Mode allowance plus monthly credits; paid agent work billed by effort Deployments billed on usage Free; Core $18/month billed yearly ($20 monthly)


Zite Internal tools with many users Flat plan, no per-user fees, credits for AI work Export moves a whole workspace, not one app Free; Pro $20/month billed annually


Base44 (for reference) Prompt-built apps with backend included Two meters: message and integration credits GitHub sync starts on Builder Free; Starter $16/month billed yearly ($20 monthly)


We built Awesomic Studio, so it's listed first. The other six aren't ranked against each other. Lovable comes first as the closest swap. Softr, Glide and Bubble follow as no-code builders, then Replit for code a developer inherits, then Zite for internal tools with many users.


We left out code-first tools such as v0, Cursor and Bolt, because they hand you a codebase to run, which is the job a no-code builder exists to spare you.


### 1. Awesomic Studio


**Best for:** Business dashboards with expert backup


**Overview:**[Awesomic Studio](https://www.awesomic.com/studio/) is our AI workspace, where agents (Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode) build what you describe, from a site or app to a deck or video. You give it text, files or links, and it publishes the result to a live URL you can keep private to your team.


Studio comes from the Awesomic team (Y Combinator, Summer 2021 batch), and it extends our design service rather than replacing it: any project can pull in an Awesomic designer or developer.


Its four setups decide how much of that help you use. Self-serve is you and the agents, and Assisted adds a specialist who reviews the work. Dedicated gives you "a vetted specialist or multi-skill team for ongoing work," and they own delivery. Automated turns recurring jobs into workflows anyone on the team can run.


**Key features:**


- The fee and the agent budget are the same figure, so there's one number to track.
- The Dedicated setup hands ongoing work to a vetted expert or team.
- Built-in hosting gives an internal dashboard a live address, private or public.
- Scheduled automations run refreshes, reports and updates after you close the tab.
- Eight connections, from Slack and Google Drive to GitHub and Figma.
- Export to code or other tools when a developer takes over.


**Pricing:** Basic is $20 a month, Pro is $200 and Maximum is $500, and the fee itself is the month's agent budget. Studio doesn't publish how fast a model or agent draws that budget down. Our Assisted and Dedicated setups are priced apart from these plans.


**Pros:** A usage budget equal to the plan price, one meter instead of two, a dedicated expert (quoted separately) in the same workspace, hosting included, scheduled automations


**Cons:** No built-in database or user logins claimed, so records and sign-ins need another tool, no published draw-down rate, and no free plan or trial, unlike every other entry here


**How to start using it:**


1. Pick Basic to test one dashboard, then Pro once the $20 budget runs short.
2. Describe the screen and upload the spreadsheet it should show.
3. Ask for changes in plain words until the build is right.
4. Publish privately to your team first.
5. Move to the Dedicated setup once the work needs an owner.


**Why it's a good Base44 alternative:** It replaces Base44's two meters with one budget equal to the plan price. When a prompt stops being enough, a person steps in without you leaving the workspace.


**Final verdict:** Choose Studio for dashboards and reporting screens where you want one monthly budget and an expert within reach. If your app's core is a database with logins, keep that part on a builder that includes them.


### 2. Lovable


**Overview:** Lovable is the nearest like-for-like swap. You describe an app, and it builds the interface along with a backend from its Cloud service, which includes a database, storage, auth, realtime and edge functions.


Its pricing still runs on credits, but on one meter: credits cover building, Cloud hosting and in-app AI together. A message in Default Mode costs 0.5 to 1.7 credits in Lovable's own examples, and Plan Mode costs 1.


**Key features:**


- Two-way GitHub sync on every plan, Free included, so the code can leave whenever you connect a repository.
- Cloud backend with database, auth and storage, the same bundle Base44 gives you.
- Unlimited users on paid plans instead of per-seat pricing.


**Pricing:** Pro costs $25 monthly or $21 a month billed yearly, with 100 monthly credits, custom domains and credit rollover. Business is $42 billed yearly or $50 monthly and adds SSO.


**Pros:** Code sync from the free plan up, one credit meter instead of two, rollover and top-ups


**Cons:** Credits on monthly plans expire 2 months after issue, code sits inside Lovable until you sync it, and free-plan apps created since May 13, 2026 are limited to 1,000 server requests per 10 seconds per project


**Where it fits:** Teams that like how Base44 builds but want the code in their own GitHub repository from day one.


**Final verdict:** The smallest change of habit on this list, with GitHub sync from the free plan rather than from Builder.


### 3. Softr


**Overview:** Softr builds portals and internal tools on top of data you may already keep: Softr Databases, Airtable, Google Sheets, Notion or SQL. Its AI Co-Builder generates pages, the database, permissions and workflows from a prompt.


Its pricing is easy to predict. AI credits pay only for AI features, including the Ask AI assistant inside your app. They reset monthly, and when they run out the AI features pause and you aren't charged.


**Key features:**


- Connects to Airtable, Google Sheets, Notion and SQL, so the records can stay where your team already edits them.
- User logins, with SSO on Enterprise, and SOC 2 Type II.
- Unlimited apps, databases, workflows and forms even on the free plan.


**Pricing:** Basic costs $19 a month billed yearly or $25 monthly and adds a custom domain with 10 AI credits. Pro is $99 billed yearly or $119 monthly, with 50 credits, branding removed and custom code and API connectors.


**Pros:** A bill that doesn't move when credits run out, data that can live outside Softr, up to 3 builders on Free


**Cons:** Basic allows only 5 team and 5 client app users, no app code export that we could find, only 5 AI credits a month on Free, installable mobile apps only as a PWA on Business ($329 billed yearly)


**Why buyers shortlist it:** The lock-in sits in the interface rather than the data, because your records can stay in Airtable or a SQL database you already run. A portal that is mostly charts may need one of the[data visualization tools](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/data-visualization-tools) for its reporting layer more than it needs an app builder.


**Final verdict:** A safe bet for a portal or internal tool whose data already lives in a spreadsheet or database.


### 4. Glide


**Overview:** Glide's new product, GlideOS, has been in open beta since July 2026. It's a chat-based builder for internal business apps that starts from a spreadsheet, a prompt or a file. The older product, Glide Classic, now sells as a separate subscription, with Business from $199 a month billed yearly.


Glide charges credits for AI work, and a Glide staff member put it plainly: "Every prompt consumes credit."


**Key features:**


- Builds from a spreadsheet you already have, so field teams can keep their familiar columns.
- One Postgres-compatible project database, plus connections to an external SQL database.
- Pro adds MCP, so you can build from your own AI agent.


**Pricing:** Basic is $25 a month with 100 credits, 2 team members and 2 published apps, and Plus is $50 with 250 credits, 3 members and 5 apps. GlideOS bills monthly only, and its pricing page offers no annual option.


**Pros:** A spreadsheet-first start, a real SQL option, plan prices that state the app count up front


**Cons:** GlideOS is still in beta, the free plan publishes no apps, and Google Sheets data comes in one way only


**What it's good at:** Turning a working spreadsheet into an app your field or ops staff can use, without a developer.


**Final verdict:** Good for small internal apps, as long as the 2 to 5 published apps on Basic and Plus cover your plans.


### 5. Bubble


**Overview:** Bubble is a full visual builder that makes web apps and, through React Native, native iOS and Android apps from the same editor. Publishing to the app stores needs a Mobile or Web & Mobile plan, from $42 a month billed yearly; the $29 Starter below is web only.


Its bill has three parts: a flat plan, AI credits and workload units, which measure the server work your app does. Bubble says "app generation does not require credits," and you can switch off overages in settings on paid plans.


**Key features:**


- Native mobile apps beside the web app, with store screens you can design before the build or hand to[mobile app design services](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/mobile-app-design-services) .
- Database export to CSV, one data type at a time, from the App data section.
- SOC 2 Type II.


**Pricing:** Starter costs $29 a month billed yearly (Bubble says yearly billing saves up to 20%), with 1,000 AI credits, 175,000 workload units and a custom domain. Growth is $119 a month billed yearly.


**Pros:** Web and native mobile in one tool, AI app generation outside the credit meter, overage controls


**Cons:** No source-code export, since apps run on Bubble's own runtime, paid AI credits expire 6 months after purchase, and the free plan can't publish a live site


**Its real strength:** Bubble suits the day an internal tool turns into a product customers pay for, because it handles both web and mobile without a rewrite.


**Final verdict:** Pick Bubble for a customer-facing app you expect to grow, and accept that it stays on Bubble.


### 6. Replit


**Overview:** Replit's Agent builds an app from a prompt and runs it with built-in hosting, a database and auth, which is why it belongs in a business-app list where code-first editors don't. The difference from Base44 is that you're always one click from the actual code.


Its docs describe a "Download as zip" option on the file tree and two-way GitHub sync through the Git pane.


**Key features:**


- Everyday agent work runs on a Free Mode allowance, and paid agent work is billed by effort, so small fixes cost less than big builds.
- Budget limits and alerts to stop a long session from emptying the month.
- Monthly credits also cover publishing, storage and databases.


**Pricing:** Core is $20 monthly or $18 a month billed yearly, with up to 30 hours of chat on Free Mode plus $20 a month in credits for more powerful models, up to 5 collaborators and unlimited published apps. Pro is $90 billed yearly or $100 monthly, with 15 collaborators and credits that roll over for 2 months.


**Pros:** The code is yours to download or sync, spending caps you can set, one platform from prototype to production


**Cons:** Deployments are billed on usage (outbound data, compute and requests) and Replit's own pages disagree on the base fee, Plan Mode can bill reasoning that changes no code, and a copied project leaves its secrets, database and deployment settings behind


**Why it made this list:** It's the exit route for a team that expects a developer to inherit the app, without giving up hosted infrastructure on day one.


**Final verdict:** Choose Replit when the app is likely to outgrow a no-code tool and you want the code ready for that day.


### 7. Zite


**Overview:** Zite comes from the company behind Fillout, which renamed itself Zite in March 2026, and it builds business apps with a built-in Zite Database. It reads and writes Airtable and Google Sheets data live, imports CSV files, and connects outward through a REST API and webhooks.


Its homepage promises "No per user fees, ever."


**Key features:**


- Credits only for AI work (building, the database agent and AI fields), with manual edits, visitors and workflow runs from the editor all free.
- Unlimited users and apps on every plan, Free included.
- Building over MCP from your own AI tool costs no credits, though after a 7-day trial it needs Business or above.


**Pricing:** Pro costs $20 a month billed annually ($240 a year), with 100+ credits, 100,000 records and one custom domain. Business is $75 a month billed annually ($900) with 400+ credits.


**Pros:** No per-seat charge as your team grows, published credit costs per action (a new page costs 1.5 to 2.25 credits), SOC 2 Type II


**Cons:** Workspace export carries code, schema, apps and forms but not records or chat history, a single app can't be exported alone, workflows in published apps draw a monthly run allowance (5,000 on Pro), and the free plan caps you at 5,000 records


**Why it works as a Base44 alternative:** Zite spends credits only on AI work and charges nothing per user, so a tool your whole company opens daily doesn't grow the bill by headcount.


**Final verdict:** A strong fit for internal tools with lots of users and a small build budget.


One Reddit reply to a Base44 user asking for options said the same: "For business apps/internal tools, Zite (maybe paired with Airtable or using zite database),"[the commenter wrote](https://www.reddit.com/r/Base44/comments/1nrrv4x/alternatives/) , steering SaaS builders toward code tools instead. It's one person's advice.


## Flat plans vs credits: what the money buys


We priced the best alternatives to Base44 in United States dollars, as each vendor's own pricing page lists them, on the cheapest paid plan. The middle column says what the plan's credits pay for, which decides how far a month stretches.


Plan Price What the credits pay for When they run out


Awesomic Studio Basic $20/month A $20 usage budget for agent work Draw-down rate per model isn't published


Lovable Pro $21/month yearly, $25 monthly 100 credits for building, Cloud hosting and in-app AI Top-ups; monthly-plan credits expire after 2 months


Softr Basic $19/month yearly, $25 monthly 10 AI credits for AI features only AI features pause, no charge


Glide Basic $25/month, billed monthly 100 credits; every prompt uses some Credit top-ups, paid plans only


Bubble Starter $29/month billed yearly 1,000 AI credits plus 175,000 workload units Overages, which you can switch off


Replit Core $18/month yearly, $20 monthly Free Mode allowance, plus $20 of credits for paid agent work, publishing, storage and databases Budget limits and alerts you set


Zite Pro $20/month billed annually 100+ credits for AI building, the database agent and AI fields Manual edits and visitors stay free; app workflows use a separate run allowance


Base44 Starter $16/month yearly, $20 monthly 100 message credits plus 2,000 integration credits Both reset monthly; unused credits expire


Sticker prices mislead here. Base44 has the cheapest yearly entry, but its integration credits are spent by the app itself, so a busy internal tool draws them down even when nobody is building.


Among Base44 alternatives, Softr and Zite keep app use off the credit meter most plainly: Softr pauses AI features instead of charging, and Zite doesn't spend credits on visitors. Each meters something else, though: Softr counts app users, and Zite counts workflow runs. Bubble and Replit add usage meters for the servers your app runs on, which matter more for a public app than an internal one.


Treat a builder's monthly fee like any recurring line in a[design project budget](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/how-to-budget-for-design-projects-as-a-startup) : price the twelfth month, not the first, because that's when the app has real users and real credit use.


## What export actually leaves you with


In a survey of UK organizations published in the[Journal of Cloud Computing](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13677-016-0054-z) , 71% of participants said vendor lock-in risks would deter them from adopting more cloud services, and 66.4% called making well-informed decisions before selecting a vendor extremely important.


App builders deserve the same scrutiny. "Export" can mean your code, your data, or neither, so the table splits them.


Tool Code out Where your data lives What stays behind


Awesomic Studio Export to code or other tools; GitHub among 8 connections You bring files and links; no database is listed No version-control claim


Lovable Two-way GitHub sync on every plan Lovable Cloud database Code stays inside Lovable until you sync


Softr No app code export found Softr Databases, or Airtable, Sheets, Notion, SQL; CSV export The interface


Glide Code viewing on Enterprise only Project database or external SQL Sheets data comes in one way


Bubble No source-code export Bubble database; CSV export per data type The whole app


Replit Zip download and two-way GitHub sync Replit databases Secrets, database and deploy settings


Zite Workspace export for import into another Zite organization Zite Database; CSV export per table Records and chat history


Base44 Two-way GitHub sync from Builder ($40/month yearly) Base44's built-in database Local runs use the Base44 CLI and a local Base44 backend


Code export and independence aren't the same thing. Base44's own FAQ says "Nothing is locked," and its GitHub sync does carry the full source, but its docs run that code locally through the Base44 CLI, which starts a local Base44 backend. Replit and Lovable give you code a developer can work on outside the platform, and Softr can leave your records in a database you already control.


## When staying on Base44 makes sense


Switching to one of these Base44 alternatives isn't always the cheaper move. Base44's Starter plan, at $16 a month billed yearly, costs less than the cheapest paid plan of any tool above, and it already includes hosting, a backend, a database, auth and a custom domain with the first year's domain free.


Manual visual edits don't cost credits, so fixing small things by hand saves them. Two-way GitHub sync arrives on Builder, at $40 a month billed yearly or $50 monthly, if a developer needs the code.


Stay if your app works, your monthly credits cover your changes, and nobody has asked where the data would go if you left. The 2025 security flaw was fixed within 24 hours, so it isn't a reason to move on its own.


If the app works but looks rough, mock up cleaner screens in one of the[app design apps](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/app-design-apps) and rebuild just those inside Base44, which is a smaller job than a move.


## How to move an app off Base44


Whichever of the Base44 alternatives you pick, plan on a rebuild rather than an import, and treat the move as a small project:


1. List every screen, table, user role and automation in the current app.
2. Export or copy your data and check the row counts against Base44.
3. Rebuild one screen on the new tool's free plan before paying for anything.
4. Recreate user roles and test sign-up on a private app with an outside email.
5. Run both apps side by side for a week before you switch users over.


Step 4 matters most for AI-built apps. The OWASP Citizen Development Top 10 ranks[Blind Trust](https://owasp.github.io/www-project-citizen-development-top10-security-risks/content/2022/en/CD-SEC-01-Blind-Trust) as its first risk, meaning platform- or model-generated output accepted without independent checking. Have someone outside the project try to get in before real records go live.


If the rebuild is also a chance to fix how the app looks and flows, a[product designer can map](https://www.awesomic.com/hire/hire-a-product-designer) the screens and roles first, so the new builder gets a clear spec instead of a copy of the old app's quirks.


## How to choose the right Base44 alternative


Start from what bothers you about Base44 today, because alternatives to Base44 app builder plans fix different problems. If it's the credit bill, pick a flat plan: Softr if your data lives in Airtable or Sheets, Zite if dozens of colleagues will use the app.


If it's ownership, pick Lovable or Replit, since both sync code to GitHub. If the internal tool is turning into a product customers pay for, Bubble covers web and native mobile in one place, and the[SaaS product design](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/saas-product-design) decisions start to matter as much as the builder.


Glide fits small teams that already run their operations from a spreadsheet.


## Which alternative to test first


Test Base44 alternatives the cheap way: rebuild one screen of your current app on two tools from the table, using each one's cheapest plan, and log the credits each spends on the same three changes. That test answers the pricing question better than any comparison page.


If the screen is a dashboard or report and you'd like an expert within reach,[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/studio/pricing) on Basic for $20 a month and give Awesomic Studio's agents that same screen; expert help is quoted separately.


## FAQ


### What are the best alternatives to Base44?


Of the Base44 competitors we compared, Lovable is the closest swap, with a built-in backend and GitHub sync on every plan. Softr and Zite suit internal tools on flat plans, Glide builds from spreadsheets, Bubble covers web and native mobile, and Replit gives you code a developer can take over.


### Which Base44 competitors have a free plan?


Lovable, Softr, Glide, Bubble, Replit and Zite all have free tiers, as does Base44. Limits vary: Glide's free plan publishes no apps, Bubble's can't publish a live site, and Replit's free app goes down after 30 days. Awesomic Studio has no free plan.


### Can you export a Base44 app and host it elsewhere?


You can sync the full source to GitHub from the Builder plan, $40 a month billed yearly. Locally, that code runs through the Base44 CLI with a local Base44 backend, so check what your app needs from that backend before planning a move.


### Is Base44 safe for internal business apps?


The July 2025 flaw Wiz Research reported, which let outsiders register on private apps, was fixed within 24 hours, and Wix found no evidence of past abuse. Whatever builder you choose, test sign-up from an outside email before storing sensitive records.


### Do credits roll over on Base44 and its alternatives?


Not on Base44: credits reset monthly and unused ones expire. Lovable rolls credits over, though monthly-plan credits expire 2 months after issue, Replit Pro rolls them over for 2 months, and Bubble's paid AI credits last 6 months from purchase.
